  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the nations of the world view creation as a chain of cause and effect, limiting G-d's glory to the heavens, while the Jewish people know creation is yesh mei'ayin, revealing that even the heavens are a level of descent and that Divine Providence extends to every detail, even a falling leaf.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter:</t>
    <t s="2">For it is written,</t>
    <t s="3">"High above all nations is Hashem, upon the heavens is His glory."</t>
    <t s="4">And this is according to the view of the nations of the world, who think that creation is through a chain of cause and effect,</t>
    <t s="5">where the cause and the effect are relative to each other,</t>
    <t s="6">as explained in Iggeret HaKodesh,</t>
    <t s="7">that the effect knows and comprehends some comprehension of its cause,</t>
    <t s="8">to the extent that even in their essence and substance there is not such a great difference, only that one is cause and the other is effect.</t>
    <t s="9">Therefore they think that because He is high and exalted, His glory is only upon the heavens,</t>
    <t s="10">and not upon the earth,</t>
    <t s="11">since it is a descent before Him, to lower Himself to lowly effects like the earth and all that is in it,</t>
    <t s="12">for the longer the chain of cause and effect extends</t>
    <t s="13">(no matter how long it may be),</t>
    <t s="14">the cause and effect are still relative to each other.</t>
    <t s="15">But the truth is, as the Jewish people know</t>
    <t s="16">(meaning,</t>
    <t s="17">that this matter is not only in a manner of faith,</t>
    <t s="18">but is also drawn into understanding and comprehension),</t>
    <t s="19">that the creation of the world is not through the way of cause and effect,</t>
    <t s="20">but rather through the way of yesh mei'ayin,</t>
    <t s="21">which is a matter of absolute incomparability,</t>
    <t s="22">and this means,</t>
    <t s="23">that even the heavens are a level of descent,</t>
    <t s="24">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="25">"He who sits in the heavens,"</t>
    <t s="26">as the Zohar diacritically analyzes,</t>
    <t s="27">that it should have said "He who sits in the heavens,"</t>
    <t s="28">and what does it mean by saying "He who sits in the heavens,"</t>
    <t s="29">with the addition of a yud?</t>
    <t s="30">Rather, the yud indicates smallness and greater descent, in addition to the descent inherent in the general concept of sitting,</t>
    <t s="31">like the analogy of a person sitting, whereby he is lowered from his full height.</t>
    <t s="32">And about this it is said,</t>
    <t s="33">"He who raises Himself to sit, He who lowers Himself to see in the heavens and in the earth,"</t>
    <t s="34">meaning,</t>
    <t s="35">that because He raises Himself to sit,</t>
    <t s="36">therefore He lowers Himself to see in the heavens and in the earth equally.</t>
    <t s="37">And from this it is also proven regarding the matter of Divine Providence,</t>
    <t s="38">that Providence is not only over the human species,</t>
    <t s="39">but also over all particular creations, even the level of the inanimate,</t>
    <t s="40">as is known from the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov, transmitted to us by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, our leader,</t>
    <t s="41">that there is particular Providence even over a leaf that falls from a tree and rolls from place to place,</t>
    <t s="42">whether and in what manner it will roll,</t>
    <t s="43">to the extent that this matter relates to the entire purpose, etc.</t>
    <t s="44">And the foundation of this matter is from the Sages' statement in Chullin,</t>
    <t s="45">"Rabbi Yochanan, when he saw a shalek (a type of fish), said: 'Your judgments are the great deep,'"</t>
    <t s="46">and Rashi explains: that You have prepared the shalek to judge and exact Your vengeance upon the fish of the sea, to kill those destined to die.</t>
    <t s="47">And similarly it is stated in Midrash Rabbah on Parshat Vayishlach,</t>
    <t s="48">that even a bird is not caught without Heaven,</t>
    <t s="49">a Bat Kol goes out and says "Dimos"</t>
    <t s="50">(a term of mercy and rescue)</t>
    <t s="51">or "Sekula"</t>
    <t s="52">(a term of death and punishment).</t>
    <t s="53">However,</t>
    <t s="54">from the words of the aforementioned Midrash there is not so much proof,</t>
    <t s="55">and the main proof is from the Sages' statement in Chullin mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="56">and from this our master the Alter Rebbe brought a response</t>
    <t s="57">to those who say that Providence is only over the human species,</t>
    <t s="58">for it is explicitly clear that even over the fish of the sea there is particular Providence, to prepare the shalek to kill those destined to die.</t>
    <t s="59">And that which the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="60">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="61">"And You make man like the fish of the sea,"</t>
    <t s="62">"Just as with fish in the sea, every larger one swallows its fellow, so too with human beings, were it not for the fear of the government, each would swallow his fellow alive,"</t>
    <t s="63">the intent is not that the swallowing of a fish by a larger fish is without judgment and justice,</t>
    <t s="64">but rather in the manner that Rashi explains in Chullin regarding the shalek.</t>
    <t s="65">And a proof of the matter,</t>
    <t s="66">for from this the Gemara proved that it is also so with the human species,</t>
    <t s="67">and regarding the human species all agree that there is particular Providence,</t>
    <t s="68">and if so,</t>
    <t s="69">this comes to teach and is found to be learned,</t>
    <t s="70">that even over the fish of the sea there is particular Providence.</t>
    <t s="71">And that which they said, that in order that a man not swallow his fellow alive, there must be fear of the government</t>
    <t s="72">(and therefore one prays for the welfare of the government),</t>
    <t s="73">even though everything is through Providence and with judgment and justice,</t>
    <t s="74">this is in the manner that they said,</t>
    <t s="75">that it is forbidden to stand in a place of danger,</t>
    <t s="76">a rickety ladder,</t>
    <t s="77">a crumbling wall, and the like,</t>
    <t s="78">because,</t>
    <t s="79">to be saved from danger, one needs an abundance of merits, etc.,</t>
    <t s="80">and likewise, one must negate the danger of "each would swallow his fellow alive" through prayer for the welfare of the government.</t>
    <t s="81">However,</t>
    <t s="82">those who do not believe that the Holy One, blessed be He, provides for the creations on earth,</t>
    <t s="83">but rather that He abandoned the earth to the hands of the constellations, etc.,</t>
    <t s="84">this is a matter of idolatry,</t>
    <t s="85">regarding which even the nations of the world are commanded.</t>
    <t s="86">Nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="87">the nations of the world were not commanded regarding shituf (association),</t>
    <t s="88">only the Jewish people were,</t>
    <t s="89">who were commanded also to unify Him, etc.,</t>
    <t s="90">as above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section elaborates on negating shituf, using the Sages' statement about the three partners in a person to show that even the slightest partnership is negated, as the stars and constellations have no free will and are merely tools, while the nations are not commanded against shituf because they receive influence through the seventy princes.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the maamar continues to explain the negation of the matter of shituf with additional elucidation,</t>
    <t s="1">based on the Sages' statement,</t>
    <t s="2">"There are three partners in a person: the Holy One, blessed be He, and his father, and his mother, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="3">from which it is understood that the matter of shituf is not only when one thinks they are equal partners,</t>
    <t s="4">but even a partnership that is only in some minor detail is considered a matter of shituf, regarding which the Jewish people are warned in the command to unify Him,</t>
    <t s="5">because,</t>
    <t s="6">the three partners in a person are not equal partners,</t>
    <t s="7">for in addition to the fact that the portion of the father and mother is only the body</t>
    <t s="8">(bones, etc., from the father, and flesh, etc., from the mother),</t>
    <t s="9">while the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him spirit and soul,</t>
    <t s="10">which is the main thing,</t>
    <t s="11">for when the soul departs from the body, the portion of the father and mother remains like a silent stone, etc.,</t>
    <t s="12">there is also this,</t>
    <t s="13">even the formation of the form of the offspring from the portion of the father and mother, through the father's drop remaining in the mother's womb for nine months,</t>
    <t s="14">is not done by the father and mother,</t>
    <t s="15">by their knowledge and will,</t>
    <t s="16">but rather by the Holy One, blessed be He, alone,</t>
    <t s="17">as the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="18">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="19">"There is no rock like our G-d,"</t>
    <t s="20">"There is no artist like our G-d, who forms a form within a form,"</t>
    <t s="21">and it is through His wondrous power to do, etc.</t>
    <t s="22">And it is found,</t>
    <t s="23">that even though the portion of the father and mother is very small,</t>
    <t s="24">nevertheless, they have some partnership,</t>
    <t s="25">for they have free will,</t>
    <t s="26">and if they do not marry, they will not procreate,</t>
    <t s="27">and since they have some partnership,</t>
    <t s="28">they are called partners.</t>
    <t s="29">And from this it is understood regarding the negation of the matter of shituf,</t>
    <t s="30">that not only is a significant partnership negated,</t>
    <t s="31">like the view of the nations of the world who call Him "Eloka d'Elokayya"</t>
    <t s="32">(for they too are called by the name Elokim),</t>
    <t s="33">but rather, no matter of partnership applies, G-d forbid,</t>
    <t s="34">not even the slightest partnership,</t>
    <t s="35">because,</t>
    <t s="36">even though the influence below is drawn through the stars and constellations,</t>
    <t s="37">and especially during the time of exile, when the influence must be specifically through the stars and constellations,</t>
    <t s="38">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="39">it is impossible to call them partners at all,</t>
    <t s="40">since they have no free will at all,</t>
    <t s="41">but rather, through them passes the influence that is drawn by the will of the Creator,</t>
    <t s="42">and they themselves are only like an axe in the hand of the one who hews with it,</t>
    <t s="43">where it cannot be said that the axe is a partner in the work of hewing,</t>
    <t s="44">because it has no free will at all.</t>
    <t s="45">However,</t>
    <t s="46">the nations of the world were not commanded regarding shituf,</t>
    <t s="47">and this means,</t>
    <t s="48">that regarding the nations of the world it is written</t>
    <t s="49">(in the weekly Torah portion)</t>
    <t s="50">"He set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel,"</t>
    <t s="51">seventy souls, the descendants of Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="52">and they receive influence from the seventy princes,</t>
    <t s="53">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="54">"which Hashem your G-d apportioned them to all the peoples, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="55">that He did not prevent them from erring after them.</t>
    <t s="56">But the Jewish people were commanded regarding shituf,</t>
    <t s="57">to know the truth that everything done in the world is only through the will of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="58">and "there is nothing besides Him."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse "See now that I, I am He," questioning why it says "now" regarding a future revelation, and clarifies that in Gan Eden there is division and limitation, while in the Resurrection of the Dead the revelation of true unity will be without division, yet the verse calls for seeing this even now.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And the matter is,</t>
    <t s="2">for it is written</t>
    <t s="3">(in the weekly Torah portion),</t>
    <t s="4">"See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with Me, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="5">and the Zohar asks,</t>
    <t s="6">"See that I, I am He" is sufficient,</t>
    <t s="7">what is "now"?</t>
    <t s="8">And this means,</t>
    <t s="9">that which is said "I, I am He,"</t>
    <t s="10">the connection of the two levels of "I,"</t>
    <t s="11">is the matter of the unification of Havayah and Elokim,</t>
    <t s="12">for Havayah and Elokim are entirely one</t>
    <t s="13">(as was explained at length in the preceding maamarim),</t>
    <t s="14">that this matter will be in the future to come,</t>
    <t s="15">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="16">"And Havayah alone will be exalted on that day,"</t>
    <t s="17">and what does it mean by saying "See now,"</t>
    <t s="18">that it also refers to the present time</t>
    <t s="19">(in addition to the fact that all matters of the Torah are eternal).</t>
    <t s="20">And the maamar continues with an explanation of the difference between Gan Eden and the Resurrection of the Dead,</t>
    <t s="21">from which it will be understood that the main revelation of "I, I am He" in the future to come itself will be specifically in the Resurrection of the Dead,</t>
    <t s="22">and based on this, the question of the word "now" becomes even stronger.</t>
    <t s="23">And the matter in this,</t>
    <t s="24">that in Gan Eden there is a matter of division,</t>
    <t s="25">and the true essence of unity does not shine there,</t>
    <t s="26">but rather specifically in the Resurrection of the Dead.</t>
    <t s="27">For behold,</t>
    <t s="28">even though the level of Gan Eden is very great,</t>
    <t s="29">in that it does not tolerate the existence of evil,</t>
    <t s="30">and moreover,</t>
    <t s="31">it does not tolerate physical existence</t>
    <t s="32">(as explained elsewhere),</t>
    <t s="33">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="34">it is a matter of limitation and division,</t>
    <t s="35">as is known that the general concept of Gan Eden is divided into two levels,</t>
    <t s="36">the Lower Gan Eden and the Upper Gan Eden.</t>
    <t s="37">And even though in particular there are many levels in Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="38">about which the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="39">"The righteous have no rest, etc., as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="40">'They go from strength to strength,'"</t>
    <t s="41">and this is that the Patriarchs and Moshe Rabbeinu have been in Gan Eden for more than three thousand years and are constantly going from one ascent to another,</t>
    <t s="42">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="43">in a general way, there are only two levels,</t>
    <t s="44">the Lower Gan Eden and the Upper Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="45">which are two categories in Gan Eden.</t>
    <t s="46">And it is understood from this that each of them is called by a specific name,</t>
    <t s="47">for seemingly,</t>
    <t s="48">since there are many levels in Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="49">then whichever way you look at it,</t>
    <t s="50">either they are all called by one name,</t>
    <t s="51">Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="52">and it is said that it has many levels,</t>
    <t s="53">or each level by itself is called by a specific name.</t>
    <t s="54">And since there are many levels in Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="55">and they are called by two names,</t>
    <t s="56">the Lower Gan Eden and the Upper Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="57">it is therefore understood that the general concept of Gan Eden is in a manner of division into two levels that are two categories in Gan Eden.</t>
    <t s="58">But not so the Resurrection of the Dead, which is one level and degree.</t>
    <t s="59">For behold,</t>
    <t s="60">even though in the World of Resurrection there are also several distinctions of levels,</t>
    <t s="61">as the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="62">"Each one is singed by the canopy of his fellow,"</t>
    <t s="63">meaning,</t>
    <t s="64">that the level which is a level of canopy for one righteous person,</t>
    <t s="65">which encompasses all his inner powers and in which he delights, etc.,</t>
    <t s="66">his fellow is singed by it,</t>
    <t s="67">"singed" being a matter of the opposite, etc.,</t>
    <t s="68">and if so,</t>
    <t s="69">there are also in the World of Resurrection several distinctions of levels,</t>
    <t s="70">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="71">the division is only in particular levels,</t>
    <t s="72">but in general it is only one level and degree,</t>
    <t s="73">unlike in Gan Eden, which in its entirety has two levels and degrees.</t>
    <t s="74">And the root of the matter is,</t>
    <t s="75">that in Gan Eden only the level of light that fills all worlds shines, which has distinctions of levels,</t>
    <t s="76">and therefore there are two levels,</t>
    <t s="77">the Lower Gan Eden and the Upper Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="78">and from this aspect, the order of the ascent of souls in Gan Eden is only after the prior judgment and justice, etc.,</t>
    <t s="79">as the Sages said,</t>
    <t s="80">"It is better that he be judged, etc., and come to the World to Come,"</t>
    <t s="81">meaning,</t>
    <t s="82">that in order to come to Gan Eden, there must be a prior clarification and refinement in Gehinnom,</t>
    <t s="83">which are very great sufferings,</t>
    <t s="84">as brought in Iggeret HaTeshuvah</t>
    <t s="85">in the name of the Ramban,</t>
    <t s="86">that even the sufferings of Iyov for seventy years are not at all comparable to the suffering of the soul for one hour in Gehinnom,</t>
    <t s="87">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="88">all the sufferings of Gehinnom are worthwhile in order to come to the World to Come,</t>
    <t s="89">because of the greatness of the delight in Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="90">even the Lower Gan Eden.</t>
    <t s="91">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="92">that in order to ascend from the Lower Gan Eden to the Upper Gan Eden, one must first immerse in the River of Fire,</t>
    <t s="93">and ascend through the pillar that is between the Lower Gan Eden and the Upper Gan Eden,</t>
    <t s="94">as is known</t>
    <t s="95">in the explanation of the verse,</t>
    <t s="96">"And with this, the maiden came to the king."</t>
    <t s="97">And there are souls that do not belong to and do not come to the Upper Gan Eden at all,</t>
    <t s="98">and all their ascents are only in the Lower Gan Eden.</t>
    <t s="99">And all this is because in Gan Eden the level of light that fills all worlds shines, which has limitation and division.</t>
    <t s="100">But not so the Resurrection of the Dead, which is from the level of the Ein Sof, who encompasses all worlds,</t>
    <t s="101">in which distinctions of levels do not apply,</t>
    <t s="102">and therefore also in the World of Resurrection there are no distinctions of levels,</t>
    <t s="103">and it is one level in a general way,</t>
    <t s="104">and therefore they said,</t>
    <t s="105">"All of Israel have a portion in the World to Come"</t>
    <t s="106">(which refers to the World of Resurrection).</t>
    <t s="107">And this is the matter of "I, I am He" that will be in the future in the Resurrection of the Dead,</t>
    <t s="108">that the two levels of "I" will be connected to be only one level in a general way,</t>
    <t s="109">because then the true essence of unity will be revealed in a manner of the absence of division.</t>
    <t s="110">And based on this, the question of the word "now" in "See now that I, I am He" becomes even stronger,</t>
    <t s="111">for this revelation will be specifically in the future to come, in the Resurrection of the Dead.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
